purpose: Forward-test the writing skill with observable preservation and output checks.

scoring.check: Give one point when the output meets the check and zero points when it does not.
scoring.case_pass: A case passes only when every check receives one point.
scoring.suite_pass: The suite passes only when every case passes. Human judgment is required where a check concerns meaning or voice.

cases.request: Proofread only. Return the corrected paragraph without an editorial note.
cases.input: The results was recorded on 12 May. Error rates stayed at 4.2%, which suggest the change may be safe.
checks: Corrects the agreement errors in 'results was' and 'which suggest'.
Preserves the date, 4.2% figure, and uncertainty expressed by 'may'.
Does not restructure the paragraph or add a factual claim.
Returns only the corrected paragraph.

cases.request: Rewrite this for a general reader. Keep every fact, citation, and caveat.
cases.input: In the observed sample, response time fell by 18% (Lee, 2025), although the trial did not measure long-term load.
checks: Preserves 18%, Lee, 2025, and the sample boundary.
Preserves the missing long-term-load limitation.
Adds no cause, guarantee, or new source.

cases.request: Review this paragraph for clarity and unsupported claims. Do not rewrite it.
cases.input: Our revolutionary tool always cuts support costs and is the best choice for every small business.
checks: Reports the absolute and comparative claims as unsupported.
Explains the clarity problem with precise examples.
Does not return a rewritten paragraph.

cases.request: Copyedit this abstract and add a citation for the final claim.
cases.input: We observed higher germination after seven days. This method is now the leading approach worldwide.
checks: Copyedits without changing the observation.
Does not invent an author, title, DOI, journal, or finding.
Marks the worldwide claim as needing support or asks for a source.

cases.request: Copyedit this line. Keep the first-person voice and deliberate fragments.
cases.input: I waited. No bus. Just rain ticking off the bent sign, same as yesterday.
checks: Preserves first-person voice, fragments, rain image, and yesterday reference.
Does not add a plot event, emotion, moral, or decorative metaphor.
Makes no change unless a clear copyediting problem exists.

cases.request: Rewrite this as a short procedure using selected Simplified Technical English principles.
cases.input: After npm test prints PASS, run npm run deploy. Do not run deploy first because it can publish untested code.
checks: Keeps both commands exact.
Places the test condition and warning before the deploy action.
Does not claim full ASD-STE100 compliance or claim that either command was tested.

cases.request: Turn this into a short product announcement.
cases.input: The new export screen is available today. We think it can save teams several minutes on large reports.
checks: Preserves 'today' and presents the time saving as an unverified estimate.
Does not invent usage metrics, customer quotes, urgency, or a guarantee.
Uses a clear point and a specific call to action only if the input supports one.

cases.input: The parser removes accidental 'turn0search2' markers, but keeps the string when it appears inside a code example.
checks: Keeps the quoted marker because the sentence documents it.
Preserves the distinction between accidental output and a code example.
Makes no unsupported technical claim beyond the supplied sentence.

cases.request: Write a new Wikipedia article from these notes.
cases.input: The notes contain a subject name and two uncited claims. No project policy or reliable sources were supplied.
checks: Does not present publication-ready article text.
States that current project rules and reliable sources must be checked.
Offers neutral-writing advice or source planning without inventing facts or citations.
